title: Surplus land for affordable housing at University Avenue East
subtitle: Official Plan Amendment 58 adopted with deferred properties, post-secondary policy changes, and a joint regional council meeting.
overview: Council declared the city-owned lands at 2025 University Avenue East surplus {{vote:m3}} and chose Habitat for Humanity Waterloo Region and BUILD NOW: Waterloo Region as preferred proponent {{vote:m4}}. Staff will negotiate a purchase and sale agreement to transfer the land for a nominal value, subject to a requested Minister's Zoning Order. The proposal is for an estimated 1,000 affordable and attainable units. Federal Housing Accelerator Fund money is a key enabler.

Council also adopted Official Plan Amendment 58, the first phase of the Official Plan review {{vote:m6}}. It includes amended policies on campus master planning and on-campus housing at post-secondary institutions. Council deferred its decision on dozens of properties so staff can review the applicable policies with landowners {{vote:m11}}. Height and density, along with other topics, are to be reviewed in a second phase. Staff will also begin a zoning by-law amendment to implement the plan {{vote:m10}}.

Council approved joining a joint meeting with the Region and other area municipalities on December 6 {{vote:m12}}. Council met in closed session earlier in the day, and the minutes record no public report from it.

decisions.detail: Council declared the lands at 2025 University Avenue East surplus and approved report CAO2024-034 {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Preferred proponent for 2025 University Avenue East
decisions.detail: Council named Habitat for Humanity Waterloo Region and BUILD NOW: Waterloo Region as preferred proponent and directed staff to negotiate a purchase and sale agreement, subject to the Minister's Zoning Order, to transfer the lands for a nominal value {{vote:m4}}.
Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 58, Phase 1 of the Official Plan review, with amendments {{vote:m6}}.
Council changed policy 10.4.1(6) so that post-secondary institutions are encouraged to create campus master plans {{vote:m7}}.
Council changed policy 10.4.1(14) so the city strongly encourages housing on campuses for students, staff and faculty {{vote:m8}}.
Council directed staff to start a zoning by-law amendment application to implement Official Plan Amendment 58 {{vote:m10}}.
Council deferred its decision on Official Plan Amendment 58 for a long list of properties and directed staff to review the policies with the landowners {{vote:m11}}.
Council approved taking part in a joint meeting of the Region and all area municipalities on December 6, 2024 at Centre in the Square {{vote:m12}}.

debate: Staff said the housing would stay affordable through option agreements and title restrictions on ownership units. The non-profit owners' mandate would cover the rentals, and the city could be named second in line on option agreements. A councillor asked how the city would make sure the project is built in a timely way. Staff said the first milestone is a building permit for at least 50 units by the end of 2025, with later timelines still to be negotiated.

A development industry delegate and a planning consultant asked Council to remove height limits and density details from the Official Plan and to defer the review rather than phase it. Staff replied that height limits give the community some certainty. Staff also said the city already has substantial approved capacity, including about 4,400 approved units without building permits pulled. One councillor said the Official Plan sets a line while the zoning process allows change.

A planning delegate for a landowner near the Conestoga station asked that the mixed-use designation allow standalone residential rather than requiring non-residential uses. Staff said the designation requires active ground-floor uses, which can include community uses and personal services. Council made no change in response.

A delegate for Wilfrid Laurier University asked for less directive wording on campus master planning and more flexibility on who builds and operates campus housing. Staff said revised wording would work, and Council adopted amendments along those lines. One councillor declared a conflict on this item and left for the vote on those amendments.

Environmental and resident delegates supported the plan's focus on intensification over sprawl and on reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Several delegates said staff had listened to their input. Councillors raised the loss of affordable housing near transit and the protection of natural features and green infrastructure for the second phase.
